additional_concerns: The executable tests an externally supplied classification that a paragraph 14 demonstration request exists; it does not establish that fact. No actual request or provider-specific scope evidence is supplied.
TRUE denotes activation only, not satisfactory demonstration or compliance. FALSE leaves unconditional confirmation and substantive responsibilities intact.

Footnote 5 can be read as elaborating paragraph 14's request-conditioned demonstration or as stating an independent, unqualified demonstration expectation. The literal question about whether a request occurred does not resolve that alternative.
Paragraph 16 concerns a separate request for a satisfactory legal opinion. Neither that request nor paragraph 15's audit request automatically establishes a paragraph 14 demonstration request.

The supplied intermediary paragraphs 17–18 concern due diligence and satisfaction with controls under their own activity conditions. Their referenced Appendix Parts A and B are missing; these provisions do not independently establish the paragraph 14 trigger.

SFC satisfaction most naturally qualifies demonstration, and high confidence most naturally qualifies smart-contract assurance. Broader attachment, confirmation timing and demonstration deadlines remain unresolved.
The structural tool PASS establishes neither legal fidelity nor actual request occurrence. No unsupported additional trigger restriction or permission is apparent in the two executable expressions.
